sources.claim: Example of a state rule (Washington): the registered agent address must be a physical street address in the state where the agent can accept service; PO Boxes and private or virtual mailboxes may not be used for it, though a PO Box may be listed as a separate mailing address. Other states have their own rules.

sections.skill: Tell apart the registered agent, mailing and physical addresses

questions.prompt: Which address receives official legal papers?

choices.text: The mailing address used for catalogs and bills
The address of the owner's favorite supplier
The address printed on the shipping boxes
The registered agent address

questions.intro: A business can have different addresses for different jobs. The REGISTERED AGENT ADDRESS is where official legal papers are delivered; states usually require a physical street address in the state. The MAILING ADDRESS is where ordinary letters and bills go; it may be a PO Box in many cases. The PHYSICAL (or principal) ADDRESS is where the business actually operates. Some addresses appear in public state records, so a home-based owner may prefer not to use her home for every one. Each state sets its own rules; Washington, for example, does not allow a PO Box as the registered agent address.
questions.feedback: The registered agent receives legal papers.
